chapter: Joe Liggins and back to Kid Ory
title: Raphael Mendez and Herb Alpert sitting in
summary: Joe tells how trumpet virtuoso Raphael Mendez sat in at the Beverly Cavern and Ory said he played too many notes, a view Barry shares about Herb Alpert.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: No. We didn't go out together anyway. I always really went my way. I remember one time, though... Once in a while, musicians, a famous musician would come up to Beverly Cavern, where we played, and the owner would let them sit in. I can't really pinpoint, except one of the highlights was Raphael Mendez. I don't know if you know who he is...
He was one of your great trumpet virtuosos. I knew his manager, and one time his manager

said, "Hey, do you think..." He said, "Rafe is crazy about this kind of music, and he'd like to try to play some of it." And he said, "Do you think Kid Ory would let him sit in and try?" I said, "I think he would." Because Ory admired him, too. Because the guy was really an artist. And I think he used to let guys sit in on a Monday night if they wanted to -- if they could play. And old Raphael Mendez brought his trumpet up there, I'll never forget it. He wanted to play "Basin Street Blues" the first thing! [LAUGHS] And you never heard so many notes flying around in your life! Ory says, "That fella's all right, but he plays too many notes." [LAUGHS]
Strangely enough, I was in New Orleans one time, and you know this boy who's got the Tijuana Brass, Herb Alpert or whatever his name is...?
He came down there and sat in with Kid Thomas' band. And it was a sad thing. Everybody in the band said, "Well, he's all right, but he blows all over the place and no lead..."
Those New Orleans guys just like a straight lead, and then improvise in the solos, and that's about it.
He cannot improvise. Because I met him through his trombone player. I knew him... He says, "Herb thinks he can, but he can't improvise. He'd like to." But he's a studio man. He can read.
